newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends weaker and near lows.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends weaker and near lows.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures ended weaker and near the bottom of the day's trading range after the market retraced gains made during the previous session.

The benchmark October contract settled 0.14 cent weaker at 11.16 cents per lb, having ranged from 11.31 to 11.15 cents. Second-position March ended 0.12 cent lower at 11.35 cents, while the rest of the board finished down 0.04 to 0.04 cent.

Some of the funds, who lifted the market to two-week highs on Wednesday, took profits from the outset when the October contract failed to reach its upside target of 11.35 cents. Commission house selling was also noted throughout the day.
The front month held over support at 11.20 as producers remained early buyers. But the buying dried up once the front month took out support and and October slipped to the day's low of 11.15 cents.
Prices are expected to ease further on Friday, market sources said, pointing to today's close near the lows and a dearth of bullish fundamental news.
"We could see lower prices tomorrow based on the close and the overall performance," Tony Passimenti, a sugar broker with Merrill Lynch, said.

He said fund selling should remain light so long as the October contract holds around 11.15 cents. "But if we come down another 10-15 points from here we could see (the funds) tossing in the towel," Passimenti said.
An estimated 14,510 lots changed hands on the day compared with Wednesday's official 34,473 lots.
Open interest in the benchmark October contract rose by 1,641 lots to 92,990 lots as of Wednesday. March gained 2,081 lots to stand at 45,826 lots.
